To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the influence of linker in the regulation process of multidomain allosterism is determined by the effective local concentration of the allosteric ligand [B]0; (2) the linker length is the key determinant of [B], and the linker flexibility has only a secondary effect on [B]0 in a narrow [B]0 window.

the linker length and flexibility determine the local concentration of allosteric ligand, and the local concentration is the essential factor to decide the open or closed state of the multidomain proteins.
the linker length is the practical determinant of the effective local concentration [Bo] of a disordered linker, and [Bo] determines the relative stability of the closed state versus the open state.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of disordered linkers in the regulation of protein activity.
the essential role of the linkers in allosteric proteins.
the effect of linker length and flexibility in the regulation of weak binding partners.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the linker can be used to favor either the closed or the open state of a multidomain protein.

disordered linkers in allosteric regulation can favor either the open or the close state, but the effect is not universal, and depends on the detailed structure of the protein system and the length of the disordered linker.
a flexible linker with a length of 40–60 amino acids would be optimal to regulate the binding of weakly interacting domains.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a flexible linker with proper length can be used as a molecular ruler for weakly interacting partners to achieve a desired binding affinity.
the linker length and flexibility are important determinants of the linker's effect on the domain–domain interaction.
disordered linkers can favor either the closed or open state of a multidomain protein, depending on the linker length and its flexibility, and the domain–domain binding affinities.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a linker with a proper length and flexibility is a key element in the regulation of weak binding partners.
the linkers can play an essential role in the regulation of the binding affinity between the domains, and thus, the linkers can be used to fine‐tune the allosteric regulation process.
disordered linkers can act as a molecular switch to control the binding of two domains.
